question: Can a language model that combines local context, transformer-XL short-term memory and a kNN long-term memory through a learned gate beat kNN-LM style output interpolation?
hypothesis: Encouraging each component to focus on a specific function (long-term storage, extended context, local information) facilitates easier training that produces an overall better language model.
contributions: SPALM: transformer with short-term cache and kNN long-term memory combined by a context-dependent gate
Experiments on WikiText-103, WMT and enwik8 against transformer, transformer-XL and kNN-LM
Analysis of neighbours, outputs, gate values and number of neighbours

method.summary: SPALM trains a transformer-XL whose final hidden state is mixed by a sigmoid gate with an attention-pooled embedding of the k nearest-neighbour next tokens retrieved (ScaNN) from a frozen datastore with one entry per training token. Keys come from a separately pretrained vanilla transformer LM; only the gate vector w_g is new.

datasets.name: WMT (built by authors from English WMT 2019 news)
datasets.split: Jan-Oct articles train, part of November dev, part of December test
datasets.preprocessing: dev/test sampled in chronological order to about 1M tokens each

models.name: SPALM (WikiText-103)
models.init_from: keys from separately pretrained vanilla transformer LM
models.context: sequence length 512; short-term memory M=512 train, 512 or 3072 test

models.name: SPALM (WMT)
models.context: sequence length 512; memory 512 train and eval

models.name: transformer, transformer-XL, kNN-LM
models.architecture: same sizes as SPALM per dataset

other.kNN-LM: transformer-XL p_LM interpolated with p_kNN, lambda tuned from {0.05,0.1,0.2,0.3,0.4} on dev (WikiText-103)

training.objective: log likelihood of the corpus (next-word prediction)
training.wall_clock: nearest-neighbour precompute: 6-8 hours for WikiText-103 and enwik8 on 1,000 CPUs, 18 hours for WMT on 9,000 CPUs

other.keys: frozen, not updated; neighbours precomputed per training token
other.value_encoder: word embedding matrix, updated in training

inference.retrieval: k nearest neighbours by max inner product search (ScaNN) over one entry per training token; k=4 word-level, 2 character-level; static evaluation (datastore not grown with eval data)

baselines: published numbers: Transformer-XL, Adaptive Input, Compressive, Longformer
eval.protocol: Wilcoxon signed-rank test on log-likelihood difference, p < 0.05, for SPALM(+kNN) vs transformer-XL; no seeds reported

availability.data: WMT 2019 public site; WikiText-103 and enwik8 public

evidence.quote: All models are trained on 128 Tensor Processing Units until convergence with batch size 256.

results.table: Table 2, M=512 rows kNN-LM (18.1 dev, 18.5 test) and SPALM (17.9 dev, 18.8 test)

results.claim: On WMT SPALM beats kNN-LM and transformer-XL on test perplexity.
On WMT kNN-LM dev perplexity (13.1) is far better than its test (15.2), a dev/test gap SPALM shows less (13.0 vs 14.0).

results.quote: kNN-LM that relies on tuning λ on the dev set is more sensitive to performance discrepancy between the dev and test sets

results.claim: On enwik8 SPALM gets 1.00 BPC while kNN-LM (1.02) underperforms transformer-XL (1.01).
Nearest-neighbour precompute for training is the main cost.

results.quote: it takes 6-8 hours to obtain neighbors for WikiText-103 and enwik8 with 1,000 CPUs and 18 hours for WMT with 9,000 CPUs

results.claim: Perplexity on WikiText-103 dev barely changes for 1 to 4 neighbours and degrades at 8 and 16.
results.quote: We see that using one nearest neighbor is enough to obtain good performance, with a slight advantage when we use four neighbors

results.claim: The retrieval encoder returns the exact next token as first neighbour on 33%, 44% and 70% of dev tokens.

results.quote: It retrieves the exact output token as the first neighbor 33%, 44%, and 70% on WikiText-103, WMT and enwik8 development sets respectively
results.note: verbatim text has a line break between 'first neighbor' and '33%'

results.claim: On enwik8 the gate values concentrate near 1 (mostly local context); on WMT they are less concentrated.
results.quote: On enwik8, the gate values are concentrated around 1.

limits: Needs neighbour retrieval for every training token (6-8h on 1,000 CPUs, 18h on 9,000 CPUs).
Keys are frozen and not trained end-to-end; end-to-end training left to future work.
Static evaluation only: datastore is not grown with eval data and dynamic-evaluation models are not compared.
Only language-modeling perplexity/BPC; no QA, generation or downstream task; no seeds or variance beyond a Wilcoxon test.
On WikiText-103 test, kNN-LM (18.5) beats SPALM alone (18.8) at M=512; the gain needs added p_kNN interpolation.
Analysis examples are cherry-picked (Fig 2) and the authors caution against reading the gate heatmaps.
No Chinese Gigaword or retrieval-augmented QA experiment; learning rate, schedule and warmup are not stated.
